instruction.text: Build the portrait of King Xerxes.

feedback.finish: Darius I’s son, Xerxes, continued the invasion of Greece after Darius died of natural causes.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: When Xerxes launched his invasion of Greece in 480 BC, he brought a huge army of around 200,000 soldiers. This meant that his army had to move very slowly, which gave the Greek city-states time to prepare.
The Greek armies, led by the Spartan King Leonidas, decided to fight the Persians at a place called Thermopylae, where a narrow pass by the mountains would allow them to hold back the Persian army.
With only 7,000 soldiers, the Greeks were heavily outnumbered. By fighting in such a narrow space, they could limit the Persian advantage.

atoms.a: Where did the Greeks fight the Persians?
How many soldiers did the Greeks have at Thermopylae?

instruction.text: This is the site of the battle of Thermopylae. Select the correct parts of the battle.
instruction.sound: This is the site of the battle of Ther-mop-ily. Select the correct parts of the battle.

feedback.correct: This was the only way through the mountains to reach the other side of the Greek lines. The Greeks thought the Persians didn’t know about it, so they only put a small defensive force there.

atoms.a: Greek accounts say there were millions of Persians at Thermopylae. Do you think this is true?

feedback.finish: Historical sources can be unreliable, as their writers sometimes lied to make themselves look good. Modern historians think there were actually about 200,000 Persians at the battle.

instruction.text: What is happening in the battle? Select the correct answer.

b.sound: The Greeks are holding off the Persian army
The Persians are attacking the mountain pass.
The two armies are negotiating for peace.
The Greeks are making their last stand.
The Greeks are winning the battle.

feedback.end: The Greek defence at Thermopylae failed when a Greek traitor told Xerxes about the mountain pass, and they were surrounded by the Persians.

instruction.text: Find the correct parts of this Greek trireme.

hint.label: Trireme
hint.text: A trireme was a Greek warship. The Athenians were famous for the quality of their fleet.

feedback.finish: While the Athenian fleet was smaller than the Persian fleet, they were very good at naval warfare.

instruction.text: Drag the trireme to the location of the final battle.

feedback.end: The defence of Thermopylae gave the Greek navy time to gather at Salamis, where they defeated the Persian navy to finally win the war!
